title: Attenuation of fibroblast activation and fibrosis by adropin in systemic sclerosis.
authors: Liang, Minrui; Dickel, Nicholas; Gyorfi, Andrea-Hermina; SafakTumerdem, Bilgesu; Li, Yi-Nan; Rigau, Aleix Rius; Liang, Chunguang; Hong, Xuezhi; Shen, Lichong; Matei, Alexandru-Emil; Trinh-Minh, Thuong; Tran-Manh, Cuong; Zhou, Xiang; Zehender, Ariella; Kreuter, Alexander; Zou, Hejian; Schett, Georg; Kunz, Meik; Distler, Jorg H W
one_liner_zh: 该文研究adropin在系统性硬化症中抑制成纤维细胞活化和纤维化的作用，虽用机器学习但核心是纤维化病理机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，仅涉及GLI1转录网络和ChIP-seq，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Fibrotic diseases impose a major socioeconomic challenge on modern societies and have limited treatment options. Adropin, a peptide hormone encoded by the energy homeostasis-associated (ENHO) gene, is implicated in metabolism and vascular homeostasis, but its role in the pathogenesis of fibrosis remains enigmatic. Here, we used machine learning approaches in combination with functional in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize adropin as a potential regulator involved in fibroblast activation and tissue fibrosis in systemic sclerosis (SSc). We demonstrated consistent down-regulation of adropin/ENHO in skin across multiple cohorts of patients with SSc. The prototypical profibrotic cytokine TGFbeta reduced adropin/ENHO expression in a JNK-dependent manner. Restoration of adropin signaling by therapeutic application of bioactive adropin(34-76) peptides in turn inhibited TGFbeta-induced fibroblast activation and fibrotic tissue remodeling in primary human dermal fibroblasts, three-dimensional full-thickness skin equivalents, mouse models of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis and sclerodermatous chronic graft-versus-host-disease (sclGvHD), and precision-cut human skin slices. Knockdown of GPR19, an adropin receptor, abrogated the antifibrotic effects of adropin in fibroblasts. RNA-seq demonstrated that the antifibrotic effects of adropin(34-76) were functionally linked to deactivation of GLI1-dependent profibrotic transcriptional networks, which was experimentally confirmed in vitro, in vivo, and ex vivo using cultured human dermal fibroblasts, a sclGvHD mouse model, and precision-cut human skin slices. ChIP-seq confirmed adropin(34-76)-induced changes in TGFbeta/GLI1 signaling. Our study characterizes the TGFbeta-induced down-regulation of adropin/ENHO expression as a potential pathomechanism of SSc as a prototypical systemic fibrotic disease that unleashes uncontrolled activation of profibrotic GLI1 signaling.
abstract_zh: 纤维化疾病对现代社会构成了重大的社会经济挑战，且治疗选择有限。Adropin，一种由能量稳态相关（ENHO）基因编码的肽激素，与代谢和血管稳态有关，但其在纤维化发病机制中的作用仍不明确。在此，我们结合机器学习方法与功能性体外和体内实验，将adropin表征为系统性硬化症（SSc）中参与成纤维细胞活化和组织纤维化的潜在调节因子。我们证明，在多个SSc患者队列的皮肤中，adropin/ENHO表达持续下调。典型的促纤维化细胞因子TGFbeta以JNK依赖性方式降低adropin/ENHO表达。通过治疗性应用生物活性adropin(34-76)肽恢复adropin信号传导，进而抑制了TGFbeta诱导的原代人真皮成纤维细胞中的成纤维细胞活化及纤维化组织重塑、三维全层皮肤等效物、博来霉素诱导的肺纤维化小鼠模型和硬皮病样慢性移植物抗宿主病（sclGvHD），以及精密切割的人皮肤切片。敲低GPR19（一种adropin受体）消除了adropin在成纤维细胞中的抗纤维化效应。RNA-seq表明，adropin(34-76)的抗纤维化作用在功能上与GLI1依赖性促纤维化转录网络的失活相关，这通过培养的人真皮成纤维细胞、sclGvHD小鼠模型和精密切割的人皮肤切片在体外、体内和离体实验中得到了实验证实。ChIP-seq确认了adropin(34-76)诱导的TGFbeta/GLI1信号传导变化。我们的研究将TGFbeta诱导的adropin/ENHO表达下调表征为SSc（一种典型的系统性纤维化疾病）的潜在病理机制，该机制释放了促纤维化GLI1信号传导的失控激活。
